title: Forced to Be Active: Evidence From a Regulation Intervention
authors: Petter Bjerksund; Trond Døskeland; André Wattø Sjuve; Andreas Ørpetveit
eligible_reason: Single common treatment date, not staggered. The Norwegian FSA intervention against closet-index funds is coded with fixed windows for all funds (create_reg_data in scripts/utils.R line 850: pre 2012-01..2013-12, event 2014-01..2015-12, post 2016-01..2019-12); interaction = is_scandinavia x is_after. Tables 3-5, 7-8 are a cross-sectional post difference and a 2x2 DiD on the last pre-date and first post-date (do_reg_diff, do_reg_did, lines 1016-1031); Table 6 is felm(alpha_gross ~ interaction + log size, log age, active share, log fee | fund_id + date) with time-varying controls. The package ships pseudo data.
design_notes: R (stats::lm, lfe::felm). Closet-index funds (active share < 40% / < 50%) in Norway vs other Scandinavian funds; outcomes active share, fees, gross alpha, sub-portfolio active share/alpha, concentration.

specs.exclusion_reason: single common post date (2016-01); two-period 2x2 lm without unit FE
single common post date; time-varying controls (log fund size, log age, active share, log fee)

data_files_note: README.pdf section 1-2: 'pseudo datasets' are provided in data/processed to run scripts/main_results; raw Morningstar Direct and Datastream data are licensed and not included.
data_provenance_note: README labels all shipped analysis files as pseudo data (Morningstar Direct licence).
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text or PDF; OpenAlex abstract empty). Single-date intervention and pseudo data; ineligible on design and data.
